name: THE PHOTOGRAPHER'S STUDIO
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE STOCK PORTRAIT BOX
LOOK_AT: Four dozen strangers in good collars, sold as anybody you like.
Every card the same gentleman, the same collar, the same steady gaze, on the same good card stock.
The box says FOUR DOZEN. There are thirty-one. Somebody's been buying gentlemen.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Four dozen men in Ohio, not saying anything.
Card on card, sliding, when I tip the box.
Nothing. Thirty-one men holding very still.

overrides.PICK_UP: They're twenty-five cents apiece, and I'd only be buying a stranger.

subjects.name: THE CAMERA
LOOK_AT: A plate camera on a tripod, with a black cloth over the back for the photographer's head. The brass is the best-kept thing in the room.
The lens is capped. The photographer only uncaps it for paying customers, and for dogs, once.
Brass and mahogany, and a bellows like an accordion. It would make a very sad accordion.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It's waiting for someone to hold still, which in this town could take a while.
The bellows breathing a little as the room warms.
Nothing. A camera is the opposite of an ear. It only takes what holds still.

overrides.USE: I wouldn't know which end was the front. I'd photograph my own eye.

subjects.name: THE HEADREST CLAMP
LOOK_AT: An iron stand with a clamp at the top, to hold a sitter's head still for the exposure. It looks like it would hold anything still.
It adjusts for height. It is currently set for a man exactly my height, which I find unsettling.
A small brass plate on it: PATENT APPLIED FOR. In this town, that counts as a guarantee.
LISTEN_TO: A screw creaking as I touch it. It has held a great many heads, and given every one of them a headache.
The screw, settling a quarter turn on its own.
Nothing. It holds its peace the way it holds a head.

overrides.USE: My head is fine where it is. It's the only thing in town I'm sure of.

subjects.name: THE PAINTED BACKDROP
LOOK_AT: A Grecian colonnade, painted on canvas. Through the real window beside it: mud. The colonnade is winning.
The columns are painted with a great deal of confidence and no knowledge of columns.
A sitter in front of this looks like a man who has been to Athens. Nobody here has been to Athens.
LISTEN_TO: The canvas stirring in the draft. Ancient Greece, rustling.
Canvas flexing against its frame. The Parthenon, settling.
Nothing. Greece is quieter than I'd imagined.

subjects.name: THE CHEMICALS
LOOK_AT: Brown bottles on a shelf, labelled in a careful hand. One says COLLODION, and one says POISON, and they are next to each other.
There are brown stains on the shelf in the shape of every bottle. They've been put back in exactly the same place for years.
A sharp smell, like a hospital that has been told a joke.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. A small stopper ticking in the heat. I am keeping my distance.
A tiny pop as one stopper eases.
Nothing. I've moved to the far side of the room, which helps.

overrides.PICK_UP: One of them says POISON. I don't know which of the others are just being modest.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW DISPLAY
LOOK_AT: The back of the window display, from inside: the gentleman in the good collar, facing the Lane. From here he's only cardboard.
He's propped on a little easel, at an angle chosen to catch the lamplight from the Lane. Somebody thought hard about the angle.
From the back he has no face at all, just card and a maker's stamp. The stamp is from Ohio.
LISTEN_TO: The Lane through the glass, faintly. Nobody in it is stopping to look at him.
The glass ticking as it cools.
Feet on the Lane, going past. Nobody stops for him.

subjects.name: THE SITTING CHAIR
LOOK_AT: A carved chair for sitters, with a cushion and a small table for one hand to rest on, thoughtfully. Everyone sits in the same pose here.
The cushion is flat in the middle, where a great many respectable men have sat very still.
There is a book on the little table, for the sitter's hand. The book is a ledger, and it is blank. It photographs as learning.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It has had more distinguished men in it than the territory has produced.
A creak, when I lean on the back. It disapproves of slouching.
Nothing. The chair is holding still for a picture nobody is taking.

subjects.name: THE PRICE CARD
LOOK_AT: PORTRAITS 50¢. SITTING INCLUDED. CABINET CARDS BY THE DOZEN. Somebody has added, in pencil: LIKENESS NOT GUARANTEED.
Fifty cents, sitting included. I wasn't aware sitting was ever excluded.
Under the prices, in very small print: DECEASED BY ARRANGEMENT. I'm not going to ask how that's arranged.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The card is pinned and says what it has to say.
The pin, loose in the board, ticking against it in the draft.
Nothing. It's a card. It doesn't negotiate.
